text.p: Culligan Water Technologies Inc showed it is serious about its acquisition strategy by announcing Wednesday it plans to buy Ametek Inc's water filtration business, analysts said.

"They're certainly accelerating their acquisition phase, which is a good sign," said E. Lawrence Hickey, an analyst at First Analysis Corp. "It sends a message to the market that they're serious, since previous acquisitions were much smaller," Hickey said.
Culligan agreed Tuesday to buy six European distributors and a water treatment company in Europe.
Earlier Wednesday, Culligan said Ametek would merge with one of its operating units once the Paoli, Pennsylvania-based company spins off its non-water filtration operations.
Ametek stockholders will receive Culligan common shares for their stock in a deal Northbrook, Illinois-based Culligan said is valued at $155 million.
"It's a good strategic move for (Culligan)," said Rod Lache, an analyst at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell. "Their objective has always been to expand their product line and their lines of distribution."

Lache said he thought the deal would add $0.03 a share to earnings this year and $0.05 in fiscal 1999. He said he raised his earnings estimate for fiscal 1998 to $1.73 from $1.70 and for fiscal 1999 to $2.10 from $2.05.

Lache said the deal would help Culligan achieve its goal of marketing its water purification products through more distribution channels, since 30 percent of Ametek's units sell to the do-it-yourself market.
"They also sell through independent water treatment dealers, commercial and industrial users and to wholesale plumbing supply companies," Lache said
Lache said the deal instantly expands Ametek's access to international markets, which currently contribute about 15 percent of its annual revenues.
Davis Manthey, an analyst at Robert W. Baird & Co Inc, said Culligan is strengthening its position in a multi-billion-dollar industry that is highly fragmented.
"There's really no Intel or Microsoft of the water industry, but Culligan is certainly a leader in consolidation," he said.
Culligan shares closed up 1 Wednesday at 37-3/8.
